components.name: Primary Action
components.description: The single current safe next action.

components.name: Secondary Action
components.css: .ds-secondary { min-height:44px; padding:9px 12px; border:1px solid #bdc6bf; border-radius:8px; background:#fbfcfa; color:#205f48; font:700 12px Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif; } .ds-secondary:hover { background:#edf3ee; } .ds-secondary:focus-visible { outline:3px solid #7fa58f; outline-offset:2px; }

narrative.overview: NetworkPilot should feel like a quiet, well-made writing and relationship workspace: private, evidence-aware, and purposeful. The interface uses a restrained editorial hierarchy, warm neutral surfaces, and deep green actions so people and messages dominate while provider mechanics recede. Density is useful only when it shortens daily work. The system favors two-pane review, one visible next action, progressive disclosure for methodology, and clear recovery states.
keyCharacteristics: Calm warm-neutral surfaces with a rare deep-green action color.
People, message copy, and relationship state precede implementation metadata.
Compact desktop workspaces recompose into focused mobile review flows.
Safety and uncertainty remain explicit without overwhelming normal work.

rules.name: The One Action Rule
rules.body: Deep green identifies the current safe next action; do not scatter equally weighted green controls across a workspace.

rules.name: The Meaningful Warning Rule
rules.body: Amber and red communicate review, uncertainty, suppression, or danger only. They are not decorative accents.

rules.name: The Read Before Density Rule
rules.body: Decision-critical text is normal body size; tiny uppercase or monospace labels are strictly tertiary.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A permanent panel does not need a shadow merely to announce its boundary.

dos: Do keep the selected person and exact next action visible while evidence scrolls.
Do write blocked and uncertain states in plain language beside the blocked action.
Do preserve keyboard focus when opening or closing mobile detail and review views.
Do use progressive disclosure for evidence, methodology, and infrastructure health.
donts: Don't infer trust, qualification, responsibility, or actionability through visual optimism.
Don't make bucket taxonomy, provider credits, or lifecycle mechanics dominate daily work.
Don't truncate a message subject, attachment identity, or blocker without a full-text affordance.
Don't make Send look like the natural continuation of approval; it is a distinct external consequence.
